### what_to_do_first.details[1]
Sentence: Under the Health Care Act (§52) there is no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks uniform diagnostic timetable guidelines, so the county should report pathway access times and flag stalled handovers using the THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers, while the national roadmap plans cancer-specific pathway descriptions and defined access-to-care target times by 2026–2028 and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended specialist care time limits is due to be completed before the 2030 mid-term evaluation (noting that completing a recommendation is not the same as implementing it).

### what_to_do_first.details[2]
Sentence: Since patients are referred according to local instructions and a mentor insight notes that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care (while a mentor insight also notes that occupational health gets patients to specialist care faster), the county should standardise referral criteria for persistent symptoms and assign a contact person for care coordination, as the national roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and symptom-based operating models by 2026–2028 alongside guidelines on a designated care coordinator by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031.
